stimulus.text: The dot plot shows the distance, in miles, from home to school for each of 11 students at a school.

stem: Which of the following statements about the 11 data values is true?

choices.text: The mean of the distances is greater than the median of the distances.
Removing the greatest distance from the data set would not change the mean of the distances.
The median of the distances is 6 miles.
The range of the distances is 15 miles.

rationale: Read off the 11 values from the dot plot: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 15. The median is the 6th of the 11 ordered values, which is 5. The mean is the sum divided by the count: \(1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 10 + 15 = 66\), and \(66 \div 11 = 6\). Since 6 is greater than 5, the mean exceeds the median — Choice A is true (the single large value of 15 pulls the mean above the median, exactly the behavior expected for a right-skewed set). Choice D fails because the range is the maximum minus the minimum, \(15 - 1 = 14\) miles, not the maximum itself; reporting 15 is the range-as-maximum error. Choice C reports 6 as the median, but 6 is the mean — the classic swap of the two measures of center. Choice B claims the mean survives removal of the outlier, but deleting 15 leaves a sum of 51 over 10 values, a mean of 5.1; the mean is precisely the statistic an extreme value moves, while the median would barely budge (from 5 to 5).
